recent_posts.title: Tesseract & ROS-I Developer Monthly Meeting Revisit — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: A recap of two developer meetings in the ROS-Industrial ecosystem. The ROS-I Developer Meeting Americas covered new documentation for Scan and Plan Workshop and Noether repositories, Python bindings for Tesseract via NanoBind (replacing Swig), upcoming events including Automate 2026 in Chicago, and concerns about ROS 2 release processes affecting industrial users. The Tesseract Monthly Check-In focused on integrating OMPL 2.0's VAMP (Vectorized Antipodal Motion Planning) with SIMD acceleration and parallel collision checking, a 20-30% performance improvement in continuous collision checking via Cole implementation, hash-based data structure replacements for performance gains, and plans for YAML schema validation tools.

recent_posts.title: PLCnext ROS Bridge: Enabling Hardware Interoperability Between Industrial PLCs and ROS — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: The PLCnext ROS Bridge is an open-source integration layer that connects Phoenix Contact PLCnext industrial PLCs to ROS-based robotic systems. It runs as a Docker-packaged PLCnext App and provides bidirectional communication between the PLC's Global Data Space (GDS) and ROS topics via gRPC. A code-generation workflow driven by an Interface Description File (IDF) automates creation of ROS publishers and subscribers for selected PLC variables. This lets ROS developers offload deterministic control, industrial fieldbus communication (EtherCAT/FSoE, PROFINET/PROFIsafe), and functional safety to the PLC while keeping high-performance computation in ROS. The app can be deployed via CI/CD and the PLCnext Web-Based Management interface, with source code and a demo available on GitHub and the PLCnext Store.

recent_posts.title: ROS 2 in Industry: Key Takeaways from the ROS-Industrial Conference 2025 — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: The 13th ROS-Industrial Europe Conference 2025 showcased ROS 2's growing adoption in production environments. Key themes included robot controller integration challenges, safety considerations for humanoid robots, hybrid deterministic-flexible architectures, and practical deployment experiences with ros2_control and industrial protocols like EtherCAT and CANOpen. Presentations covered market growth trends, driver development, AI integration workflows, and domain-specific solutions like railway maintenance navigation. While technical progress is evident through improved interoperability and behavior-tree architectures, challenges remain in documentation quality, real-time performance, and long-term ecosystem support.

recent_posts.title: First of 2026 ROS-I Developers' Meeting Looks at Upcoming Releases and Collaboration — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: The ROS-Industrial Developers' Meeting covered updates on Tesseract (approaching 1.0 release with API improvements and plugin-based architecture), MoveIt2 community support transition, and Trajopt rewrite for better trajectory handling. Key focus areas include GPU acceleration for optimization, toolpath generation via the noether repository, and migration paths for developers. The meeting emphasized community collaboration to advance open-source industrial automation tools.

recent_posts.title: ROSCon 2025 & RIC-AP Summit 2025 Blog Series: Singapore’s Defining Week for Open-Source Robotics — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: ROSCon 2025 and RIC-AP Summit 2025 featured site tours across Singapore showcasing real-world deployments of ROS and Open-RMF in manufacturing, healthcare, and smart infrastructure. Tours included SIMTech's autonomous material handling, CHART's hospital robot fleet management, SUTD's reconfigurable robots, Changi Airport's Open-RMF integration, and Panasonic's AI-enhanced fleet management in Punggol Digital District. The events demonstrated Singapore's leadership in operationalizing open-source robotics across industries, with multi-robot coordination systems deployed in hospitals, airports, hotels, and manufacturing facilities.

recent_posts.title: ROSCon 2025 & RIC-AP Summit 2025 Blog Series: Singapore’s Defining Week for Open-Source Robotics — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: ROSCon 2025 and RIC-AP Summit 2025 in Singapore highlighted Asia Pacific's leadership in open-source robotics. Key announcements included the launch of ELEVATE @ BCA Braddell Campus, a cyber-physical testbed for validating robot interoperability using Open-RMF, with 8 companies committing to use the facility. A partnership between ROS-Industrial Consortium Asia Pacific and SGInnovate was announced to accelerate robotics talent placement through the Deep Tech Central platform. The summit featured discussions on ROS 2, Open-RMF deployments in airports and hospitals, humanoid robotics innovations, and diversity in robotics through Women in Robotics panels.

recent_posts.title: One Attendees Observations from ROSCon 2025 — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: ROSCon 2025 in Singapore brought together 1,000 attendees from 52 countries to discuss advancements in the ROS ecosystem. The conference featured workshops on MoveIt Pro, ros2_control on ESP32, and underwater robotics, alongside sessions on AI integration, motion planning, physics simulators like Mujoco, and multi-fleet coordination with OpenRMF. Key takeaways included exploring RMW Zenoh, AI-driven solutions like imitation and reinforcement learning, and Rust-based development with rclrs. The event highlighted challenges in scaling AI with multi-modal sensors and improving industrial robotics applications, with ROSCon 2026 scheduled for Toronto.

recent_posts.title: ROSCon 2025 & RIC-AP Summit 2025 Blog Series: Singapore’s Defining Week for Open-Source Robotics — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: ROSCon 2025 in Singapore brought together over 1,000 participants from 52 countries for three days of technical talks, tutorials, and demos. Key highlights included a strategic collaboration between OSRF and A*STAR's ARTC to co-develop Open-RMF best practices and interoperability standards, announcements of Singapore's national standards (SS 713 and TR 130) for robot interoperability, and the establishment of a national sandbox at BCA Braddell Campus for validation. The event positioned Singapore as a neutral hub for open-source robotics collaboration, bridging research and industry while advancing multi-vendor robot fleet deployments.

recent_posts.title: Scan-N-Plan Workshop Documentation Refresh — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: ROS-Industrial Consortium released updated documentation for their Scan-N-Plan workshop, a ROS 2-based framework for perception-driven robot trajectory planning using 3D scan data. The solution addresses challenges in industrial robotics where traditional programming methods fail, such as high part variability, missing CAD models, or deformable parts. The new documentation includes architecture diagrams, setup instructions, behavior tree customization guides, and deployment examples to help developers build industrial applications with real-time robot path planning.

recent_posts.title: New Tools for Robotics: RQT Frame Editor and the pitasc Framework — ROS-Industrial
recent_posts.summary: Two new robotics tools have been introduced: RQT Frame Editor, a ROS plugin for visual TF-frame management that eliminates manual configuration file editing, and pitasc, a skill-based framework for force-controlled assembly tasks. The RQT Frame Editor offers interactive frame manipulation, mesh visualization, and ROS service integration. The pitasc framework uses reusable skill blocks for complex assembly operations and has been deployed in industrial applications including plastic component assembly, riveting, and dual-arm coordination tasks.
